scope: Four exact whole native generated sources only: Union A SE contact/casualty and Confederate A NW contact/casualty. Source suitability and registration acceptance precede, and do not establish, runtime or local-install acceptance.
referenceMethod: For each army, independently select native cap-only and near-support-sole ROIs in the four contact cells; recompute alpha>=64 cap top and exclusive sole bottom, subtract, sort the four spans and round the midpoint median half up. Apply that one unchanged contact reference to its entire contact and casualty pair. Natural lunge/crouch/fall projection is retained without individual phase-height normalization.
pivotMethod: Choose integer X from the visually projected pelvis or prone hip center independently of the support ROI horizontal location. Choose support-specific near sole, knee, hip-side, torso or forearm ROI; integer Y must equal its exclusive alpha>=64 maximum. Weapon bounds and lifted far boots do not define later fall roots.
pairScaleJudgment: All four whole sources and sixteen native cells were inspected. Within each army pair, cap/head, blanket/pack, limb thickness and boot proportions remain coherent under changes in projection. The taller first stumble and shortened crouch/fall projections are retained; this judgment does not certify exact physical anatomy or phase-perfect motion.

rejectionSummary: The initial four sheets failed the same 16 px solid-padding boundary; the initial Confederate extension also read as a shouldered aiming pose. Subsequent unsafe-margin attempts were not rescued by alpha edits, crops, mirroring, export resizing or threshold waivers. The selected four original PNG files were independently compared byte for byte with their generated originals.
limitations: Confederate rear grips are partly occluded by torso/pack in the guard, extension and recovery; the final lowered stock and extended forearm distinguish contact from firing, but no anatomy or historical-drill certification is given.
Colored low-alpha fringe and nonzero-alpha noise remain. Solid alpha>=64 margins pass; this is not an edge/fringe-free certification.
Stylized fingers, close hand overlap, pack occlusion and single-still weight transfer remain practical limits at high zoom.
Natural pose projection and support-dependent falling roots require actual exported playback to assess timing and apparent sliding; source-only inspection does not prove every runtime phase.
Formation overlap may obscure these small figures in real play. No full-family, human usability, GPU, default-art, production/release, or whole-game quality approval is implied.
